session: v10 W12 -- modern detector on a license-clean path (master doc 5.6 item 3)
scope: DEV-20 only (the tuning split). TEST-38, test-49 and challenge are not read, extracted or scored. GPU work on a100server1 GPU 1 only, after the W11 tmux job releases it.

what_is_already_known: kb v9-w7-001: on OUR chain the detector's own image-space recall is 0.9711 at DETECT_CONF 0.20; only 9.7% of census misses have no box at any confidence; a PERFECT detector prices at +0.57 GS-DetA on the old substrate.
kb v9-w7-001: 66.1% of misses are confident boxes the chain discards after the detector.
kb v9-w7-003: writing those discarded boxes through costs -7.11 GS-DetA (recovered detections carry no attribute yield).
kb v10-frz-003: extraction drift ~1.1 GS-HOTA between runs -- SAME-WINDOW pairing is mandatory.
premise_stated_honestly.the_unmeasured_mechanism: The +0.57 ceiling prices MISSES ONLY. A modern detector changes the whole distribution: box geometry (tighter/steadier boxes -> better foot points -> better projection and crops), confidence calibration (which is what ByteTrack's activation and Kalman re-match consume -- the 66% discard bucket), role-class quality, and NMS behaviour. None of those is priced by the miss oracle. This session measures those axes; it does not assume them.

stage0_license_recon.method: LICENSE text and GitHub/HF API metadata fetched server-side (a100server1 has egress).

verdicts.Intellindust-AI-Lab/DEIMv2: LICENSE = verbatim Apache-2.0 text under an Intellindust copyright header ('DEIM is licensed under the Apache License'). GitHub reports NOASSERTION only because of the prepended header. Code: Apache-2.0. 1,982 stars, pushed 2026-08-14.

verdicts.julianzu9612/RFDETR-Soccernet: HF card license apache-2.0; weights checkpoint 1,566,066,207 bytes (1.57 GB); RF-DETR fine-tuned on SoccerNet-Tracking 2023, dataset_size 42,750 images = exactly 57 clips x 750 frames = the TRAIN split's frame count (card does not name the split -- treated as an open contamination question, tested in stage 1c).

stage0_license_recon.chosen_family_and_why: RF-DETR (Apache-2.0, DINOv2 ViT backbone, NMS-free DETR head) with the Apache-2.0 SoccerNet fine-tune as the primary arm. Reasons, in order: (1) it is already wired into this repo (generator.extract._RFDetrDetector, --detector rfdetr), so integration is a pip install, not a vendored repo; (2) the in-domain 4-class checkpoint (ball/player/referee/goalkeeper) matches our role contract exactly and needs ZERO training, which makes stage 1 a strictly stronger kill test than a COCO zero-shot arm -- if an in-domain modern transformer shows no advantage, the axis closes with more force; (3) DEIMv2 / D-FINE are equally license-clean but need a vendored repo + COCO-person-only zero-shot, so they are the FALLBACK, run only if stage 1 leaves the axis open.
stage0_license_recon.finetune_recipe_if_stage2_licenses: S4b pattern (role-as-class, single-stage, GSR-train + SoccerNet-v3 server-side) applied to RF-DETR via the rfdetr package's own train API. Two-stage (person detector + role head) is NOT chosen: our chain consumes per-detection role ids directly from the detector, and the census's dominant role error (player->referee, 7,032 rows) is a class-quality problem the 4-class head addresses in one pass.

stage1_registered_kill_experiment.substrate: DEV-20 frames (20 sequences x 750 frames = 15,000 images), img1 jpgs, GT from Labels-GameState.json.

arms_all_in_one_gpu_window.CTL_s4b_640: The shipped S4b detector (models/gsr_det/gsr_v3_ft_b_last.pt, md5 2074d8741f97a6892a1322d0f808244c) at the pipeline's imgsz 640, conf floor 0.01, iou 0.7, RGB channel order (what generator.extract feeds).
arms_all_in_one_gpu_window.CTL_s4b_1280: The same weights at imgsz 1280 -- the RESOLUTION CONTROL, so an RF-DETR win at its native 1280 cannot be booked as an architecture win when it is a pixel win.
arms_all_in_one_gpu_window.ARM_rfdetr_soccer: RF-DETR SoccerNet checkpoint at its native resolution, conf floor 0.01, same frames, same window.

stage1_registered_kill_experiment.instrument: tools/gsr_v9_w7_infer.py's dump schema (frame,image_x,image_y,x1,y1,x2,y2,conf,cls,role) is reused verbatim for the YOLO arms; the RF-DETR arm writes the identical schema. Analysis reuses tools.gsr_v9_w7.match_feet (scale-free 0.5-box-height foot gate) and tools.gsr_v9_w7.replay_tracker (CPU ByteTrack replay at the shipped c0.20/m3).

axes_and_thresholds.A_recall_at_matched_operating_point: Per arm, choose the confidence threshold at which the arm emits the same number of person boxes as CTL_s4b_640 does at 0.20; report GT-row recall there, plus recall at the fixed 0.20 and the full recall-vs-boxcount curve. ADVANTAGE = recall gain > +0.005 absolute (0.5 recall points; the control sits 2.9 points from perfect and perfect is worth +0.57 GS-DetA, so a smaller gain cannot repay a retrain).
axes_and_thresholds.B_box_quality: On matched pairs: IoU with the GT bbox_image, and foot-point error in GT-box-height units (the quantity the homography actually consumes). ADVANTAGE = median IoU +0.02 or median foot error -10% relative.
axes_and_thresholds.C_chain_discard_survival: ByteTrack replay at the shipped settings on each arm's own boxes: post-tracker GT recall and the fraction of >=0.20 boxes the tracker discards. ADVANTAGE = post-tracker recall gain > +0.005 or discard fraction lower by > 2 points at equal input recall.
axes_and_thresholds.leak_check_1c: The same recall measurement on 3 GSR-TRAIN sequences (SNGS-060, -061, -062) for CTL_s4b_640 and ARM. Both models saw train data, so this is a memorisation reference, not a clean control; a DEV-20 recall that EXCEEDS the arm's own train recall would flag the card's unnamed split as a contamination hazard and void the arm.

stage1_registered_kill_experiment.kill_rule: If ARM_rfdetr_soccer shows NO advantage above threshold on ANY of axes A, B, C against CTL_s4b_640 (with CTL_s4b_1280 used to attribute any advantage to resolution rather than architecture), the modern-detector axis CLOSES WITHOUT TRAINING and no stage 2 is run. An S4b-style fine-tune of the same family could only grow an advantage that already exists in-domain; it cannot create one that is absent at every measured axis.
stage1_registered_kill_experiment.fallback_if_axis_stays_open_but_arm_is_a: Add a DEIMv2 (Apache-2.0) COCO zero-shot person arm in the same window before any training is scheduled.

stage2_bars_if_stage1_licenses.discipline: A detector swap invalidates every downstream cache: positions, calibration re-gate, per-crop OCR, box cache, embeddings. Both arms must be extracted in ONE window (kb v10-frz-003) and both re-derived through the full chain.
bars: pooled DEV-20 GS-HOTA >= +1.0 over the same-window control, with the full shipped flag stack + arm D + s4 applied to BOTH sides
GS-DetA not worse than the control
per-sequence paired GS-HOTA helped > hurt with Wilcoxon p < 0.05 (n = 20)

amendment_1_axis_D_role_quality.when: 2026-08-17, after axes A/B/C were computed and BEFORE any role number was produced (the role code did not exist when A/B/C were read).
amendment_1_axis_D_role_quality.why: The premise in section 1 names 'role-class quality' as one of the distribution changes a modern detector brings, and section 1's axis list did not operationalise it. Role errors are the census's second-largest attribute bucket (+1.42 GS-DetA isolated, +8.13 marginal), so leaving the axis unmeasured would have understated BOTH the upside and the risk of a swap.
amendment_1_axis_D_role_quality.axis_D: On matched detections at conf 0.20, each dump's own class name against the GT role attribute: per-role accuracy and the full confusion. No pass/fail threshold was pre-registered for D; it is reported as a magnitude and used only to qualify the A/B/C verdict, never to manufacture one.
amendment_1_axis_D_role_quality.honesty_note: D is therefore a post-registration measurement. It is stated as such wherever it is quoted.

stage1_results_and_verdict.gpu_window: 2026-08-17 07:24-07:56 UTC+0530 on a100server1 GPU 1, after W11's harvest job printed HARVEST_DONE rc=0. All three dumps and both control dumps are inside that window.

axis_A_recall_at_matched_op.verdict: rfdetr FAIL (-0.00169 vs the +0.005 bar); s4b_1280 PASS (+0.01077)

axis_B_box_quality.verdict: rfdetr FAIL (IoU -0.011, foot -0.96%); s4b_1280 FAIL ON THE BARS but moves both the right way (IoU +0.012 vs a +0.02 bar, foot -7.4% vs a -10% bar)

axis_D_role_quality_post_registration.reading: the modern checkpoint is 12.05 role points worse and multiplies our dominant role error 4.5x

leak_check_1c.reading: both detectors sit ~2.4-2.8 recall points higher on GSR-train than on DEV-20, the same gap shape; no evidence that the checkpoint's unnamed split contaminates DEV-20

stage1_results_and_verdict.decision: The registered kill rule is formally NOT triggered (axis C passes for the modern detector), but the honest verdict is a KILL FOR THE DETECTOR SWAP: at our operating point the modern in-domain DETR is worse on recall (A), looser on boxes (B) and catastrophically worse on roles (D), and its single advantage (C, +0.0075 post-tracker recall / 2.1 fewer discard points) prices at ~+0.1..0.2 GS-DetA -- an order of magnitude under this session's own +1.0 GS-HOTA stage-2 bar. No stage-2 fine-tune was run and none is recommended for this family. The session hands back ONE candidate instead: the incumbent detector at imgsz 1280, which dominates its own 640 curve on every axis measured, for ~1.5x detector inference. Pricing it end to end is a separate, registered, same-window two-arm re-extraction (~5-6 GPU-h) and an orchestrator call, not a worker's unilateral spend.
stage1_results_and_verdict.gpu_hours: 0.289 GPU-h of measured inference (S4b 640 over 20 DEV + 3 train sequences, S4b 1280 over 20, RF-DETR 560 over 20 DEV + 3 train = 0.145 + 0.015 + 0.129), plus a few minutes of model loading and two smoke frames. No training, no re-extraction, no GPU scoring. All CPU analysis ran server-side on the 128-core host.
